title: Saving a life 'reward enough' for hero: Governor General to award bravery medals to four Ottawa residents
article: A couple who saved a neighbour from her knife-wielding husband and two men who led a dazed man out of a burning rooming house will receive medals of bravery from the Governor General.

Jean Charlebois and Blair Thomas, both of Ottawa, rescued a man from a burning house on Aug. 8, 2000. Mitchell and Margaret Smith of Stittsville stopped a man from stabbing his wife to death on Oct. 4, 2000.
"I guess it's not a big deal," said Mr. Charlebois of the impending award. "It's kind of nice, but there is more satisfaction in knowing you saved a couple of people. That's reward enough."

Mr. Charlebois was running errands when he heard fire alarms go off and saw smoke pouring out of a two-storey rooming house at 341 Bell St. S. Worried that someone was inside, Mr. Charlebois dashed in and out of the burning house, calling out for occupants. Moments later, another passerby, Mr. Thomas, ran into the house, while Mr. Charlebois gasped for clean air outside.
"He wasn't coming out so I started to worry he wasn't able to find his way. I opened the door and heard cries of \'Help me, help me.' "
He ran back into the house but there was so much smoke he couldn't see. "Towards the back of the building I felt someone and pulled them out."
"Them" turned out to be Mr. Thomas and a third man he was pulling out. A few minutes later, the fire department showed up.
The Smiths' ordeal last October came to a deadly end.
When Mr. and Mrs. Smith, then 71 and 69, realized their neighbour, Sally McIntyre, was being attacked with knives by her husband, Mr. Smith ran outside and tackled 35-year-old Frank Hutterer.
Mr. Smith was knocked down and stabbed in the back and chest. His wife, trying to grab the two knives from Mr. Hutterer, cut her hands before running inside to call the police.
When a police officer arrived, Mr. Hutterer ignored repeated commands to stop. The officer fired four shots before Mr. Hutterer fell dead to the ground.

Mrs. Smith and her husband said they are honoured by the Government House announcement they are to receive the medals and plan to accept them. But she doesn't want to talk about what happened that night.
"We may have saved Sally, but we lost Frank," she said. "He was a sweet, kind gentlemen. It was just one of those things that happen."
The Governor General hands out awards for bravery twice a year. No date has been set for the next ceremony, when she will hand out 11 medals for acts of heroism.
